title: Federal Jury Convicts Honduran Man in Laredo Human Smuggling Case
excerpt: A federal jury in Laredo convicted 29-year-old Honduran national Arnol Josue Flores of conspiracy to transport illegal aliens and transporting illegal aliens for profit, after a one-day trial in which the jury deliberated about two hours, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office.
content:
A federal jury in Laredo has convicted a 29-year-old Honduran national of conspiracy to transport illegal aliens and transporting illegal aliens for profit, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas.

The jury deliberated for approximately two hours before finding Arnol Josue Flores guilty following a one-day trial, the office said. Visiting U.S. District Judge Ivan Lemelle presided over the trial.

On Aug. 9, Flores picked up two people in a white Chevrolet Malibu after they emerged from the brush and crossed a fence beside a South Texas road, according to the release. He drove them for about 40 minutes before encountering law enforcement near Hebbronville.

Testimony at trial showed that one of the people Flores picked up had paid $11,000 to be smuggled into the United States and transported to Houston, where he planned to pay another $4,000 for transportation to Florida, according to the release. The man described hiding overnight in the brush before Flores picked him up the following morning.

The jury also heard that Flores failed to stop when authorities activated their emergency lights, eventually stopping at a gate, getting out of the vehicle and trying to flee on foot, according to the release. Testimony showed Flores had received a vehicle and a cell phone, followed directions, shared his location and picked up the passengers.

The defense argued that Flores was also being smuggled and drove at others' direction in exchange for transportation, according to the release.

Sentencing will be set at a later date. Flores faces up to 10 years in federal prison and a possible $250,000 maximum fine, and he has been and will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility, according to the release. Border Patrol conducted the investigation, and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Christine A. Cortez and Margaret Bernauer are prosecuting the case.

Sources: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas, Nov. 18, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026.
